# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ADR | *Architecture Decision Record*: a short record of a decision, with context, alternatives, and consequences |
| Backlog | A prioritized list of what hasn't started yet |
| Branch protection | Rules that block changes to `main` without a PR and green CI |
| CI/CD | Continuous integration (checking every change) and continuous delivery (releasing in an automated way) |
| Conventional Commits | A commit message convention with a type prefix (`feat:`, `fix:`) |
| Definition of done | Criteria a task must meet to be considered finished |
| Deploy | Releasing a version of the code to an environment |
| Docs-as-code | Documentation versioned in the repository and reviewed like code |
| DORA | Research that defined four delivery performance metrics |
| DR drill | Disaster recovery rehearsal: actually restoring the backup, in a separate environment |
| Draft PR | A pull request in draft: CI runs, but it can't be merged and doesn't request review |
| Epic | A large body of work, split into features and tasks |
| Estimate (story points) | A relative measure of a task's size and uncertainty |
| Expand → migrate → contract | A way to change the database without breaking the previous version of the code |
| Feature flag | A switch that turns a feature on or off without a new deploy |
| GitHub Flow | A flow with an always-deployable `main` and short branches through PRs |
| Iteration (sprint) | A fixed work cycle; in this book, two weeks |
| Least privilege | Each person has only the access their role requires |
| Observability | The ability to understand the system through errors, logs, and metrics |
| Postmortem | A blameless analysis of an incident, with improvement actions |
| Pull request (PR) | A request to merge a branch into `main`, with a description, CI, and review |
| Rollback | Going back to the previous version after a problematic deploy |
| RPO | *Recovery Point Objective*: how much data it's acceptable to lose in a disaster |
| RTO | *Recovery Time Objective*: how long the service can be down in a disaster |
| Runbook | A step-by-step guide for a known operational situation |
| SaaS | *Software as a Service*: software used over the internet, maintained by whoever offers it |
| Secret scanning | A GitHub feature that detects keys and passwords in commits |
| SEV | An incident's severity level (SEV1 is the most severe) |
| SOC 2 | An audit of security controls, common for SaaS sold to businesses |
| Squash and merge | A merge that combines all of a PR's commits into a single commit on `main` |
| Staging | An environment like production, with fictional data, for validating before release |
